content: 1. Stordal (2017) conducted a prospective cohort study in Norway involving 70,511 singleton infants. The study assessed the impact of breastfeeding at different ages (0–1 month, 1–3 months, 4–5 months, and ≥6 months) on morbidity outcomes, including lower respiratory tract infections (LRTI), upper respiratory tract infections (URTI), gastroenteritis, otitis media, pneumonia, and frequent infections. 2. Sit (2001) performed a retrospective cohort study in Canada with 130 healthy, full-term infants. By 4 months of age, the study compared breastfed and formula-fed infants in terms of weight-for-age, height-for-age, and weight-for-height metrics. 3. Yuan (2016) conducted a prospective cohort study in France with 268 infants, examining dietary patterns in breastfed and formula-fed infants under 6 months and those aged ≥6 months. 4. Gebreweld (2019) carried out a retrospective cohort study in Ethiopia involving 404 children aged 6–59 months. The study evaluated height, weight, underweight status, stunting, wasting, and hemoglobin (Hb) levels in children breastfed for <6 months and ≥6 months. 5. Ekelund (2021) conducted a prospective cohort study in Norway with 3,708 children aged ≥6 months. The study assessed the relationship between breastfeeding and formula feeding with atopic dermatitis, allergic rhinitis, and asthma. 6. Differding (2020a) performed a prospective cohort study in Canada with 392 healthy singleton children. The study evaluated weight, height, BMI z-scores, and gut microbiota diversity in children breastfed for ≤4 months and >4 months. 7. Differding (2020b) conducted a prospective cohort study in the United States with 67 healthy mother-infant pairs. The study examined gut microbiota diversity, composition, and short-chain fatty acid (SCFA) concentrations in infants breastfed for ≤3 months and >3 months. 8. Dhami (2019) carried out a retrospective cohort study in India with 13,548 infants aged 6–8 months. The study explored the effects of early versus delayed introduction of solid foods on stunting outcomes. 9. Tessema (2013) conducted a retrospective cohort study in Ethiopia with 575 mother-infant pairs aged 0–23 months. The study assessed the impact of pre-lacteal feeding and formula feeding on height, weight, BMI, stunting, and head circumference. 10. Malako (2018) performed a retrospective cohort study in Ethiopia with 485 children aged 6–23 months. The study evaluated hemoglobin levels in children breastfed before, at, or after 6 months. 11. Kleynhans (2006) conducted a retrospective cohort study in South Africa with 536 mother-child pairs aged 12–24 months. The study assessed height, weight, BMI, stunting, obesity, and overweight outcomes in breastfed infants. 12. Kamudoni (2015) carried out a retrospective cohort study in Malawi with 349 mother-infant pairs. The study evaluated length-for-age and weight-for-age z-scores in infants breastfed before and after 6 months. 13. Jeana (2017) conducted a retrospective cohort study in Korea with 619 infants aged 8–15 months. The study assessed height, hemoglobin levels, hematological parameters, and micronutrient status in breastfed, mixed-fed, and formula-fed infants. 14. Gingras (2019) performed a prospective cohort study in the United States with 1,013 participants. The study examined adiposity outcomes, including height, weight, BMI z-scores, waist circumference, body fat percentage, DXA trunk fat mass, and skinfold thickness, in infants breastfed for <6 months and ≥6 months. 15. Kano (2011) conducted a retrospective cohort study in Palestine with 571 preschool children aged 5–6 years. The study evaluated height, weight, BMI, stunting, overweight, and obesity in children exclusively breastfed for <4 months, 4–6 months, and >6 months. 16. Hay (2008) performed a prospective cohort study in Norway with 364 healthy full-term singleton infants. The study assessed hemoglobin levels, hematological parameters, and micronutrient levels (folate, cobalamin, holoTC, holoHC, MMA, tHcy) in breastfed infants at 6 and 12 months. 17. Sirkka (2021) conducted a prospective cohort study in the Netherlands with 3,524 infants. The study evaluated height, weight, and BMI in infants breastfed for <4 months and ≥4 months. 18. Zheng (2015) performed a prospective cohort study in China with 40,510 healthy children. The study assessed height, weight, and BMI z-scores in children breastfed for ≤3 months, 4–6 months, and >6 months. 19. Grimshaw (2013) conducted a nested case-control study in the United Kingdom with 123 infants. The study examined the relationship between breastfeeding and formula feeding with food allergies in infants ≥17 weeks versus <17 weeks. 20. Wilson (1998) carried out a retrospective cohort study in the United Kingdom with 545 infants. 21. Baird (2008) performed a prospective cohort study in the United Kingdom with 1,740 singleton full-term infants. The study evaluated height, weight, and skinfold thickness in infants breastfed or formula-fed for <3 months, 3 months, 4 months, 5 months, and ≥6 months. 22. Ejlerskov (2015) conducted a prospective cohort study in Denmark with 233 full-term singleton infants. The study assessed weight-for-age, height-for-age, weight-for-height, BMI z-scores, skinfold thickness, and body composition in infants fully breastfed at 4 months, partially breastfed at 9 months, and formula-fed at 9 months. 23. Lande (2005) carried out a retrospective cohort study in Norway with 1,441 full-term infants. The study evaluated height, weight, and BMI in infants breastfed or formula-fed for ≤4 months, 4–5 months, and >5 months. 24. Layte (2014) performed a prospective cohort study in Ireland with 9,057 participants. The study assessed height, weight, and BMI in infants breastfed for <4 months, <5 months, <6 months, and ≥6 months. 25. De Beer (2015) conducted a prospective cohort study in the Netherlands with 2,227 full-term children. The study evaluated height, weight, BMI, and body composition (fat mass, free fat mass) in infants breastfed for <4 months, 4–6 months, and >6 months.
